newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM Nov options busy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM Nov options busy.

text.p: Options on shares of International Business Machines Corp were active as investors played volatility in the stock on Monday, traders said.
By 1225 CDT/1725 GMT, IBM shares were up 2-3/4 at 132-1/8 on consolidated volume of 5.75 million shares. The stock fell as low as 126-3/4 and rose as high as 135-3/8.
The company reported third-quarter earnings that were roughly in line with analysts' forecasts.
IBM's chief financial officer told analysts during a conference call that he was "very comfortable" about the company's prospects for the rest of the year.
"IBM is crazy," Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said of trading in the computer giant's options.
The action was highlighted by the roughly 14,450 of the IBM November 130 calls that changed hands.
The November 130 call, with open interest of about 15,100 through last Friday, had the highest open interest of any IBM option.
Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities, said he saw some call buying in the morning as the stock rebounded from an opening decline and moved higher.

Todd Salamone at Investment Research Institute said that IBM shares were holding steady above the 130 strike price was "impressive," but the key will be how much of the volume translates into open interest.
He explained that if much of the volume in the November 130 calls does translate into open interest, a break below that level would be bearish but call-related support should emerge at that level.

"One thing I don't like is the volume in the 135 and 140 calls," he added. "As far as today, you don't like to see that out-of-the-money activity with the stock reversing lower off its (intraday) high.
"But again, you have to analyze it on a closing basis," he said, adding that often stocks will get a late-session boost as so-called "smart money" buys the morning dip.
The IBM November 135 call, which had open interest of about 7,340, traded 8,880 contracts and the 140 call, with open interest of 5,385, traded 7,230 contracts.
Marty Kearney of PTI Securities said volatilities in the November calls were in the 30's, down from last week.
On the put side, the IBM November 125 was most active, with more than 3,900 contracts changing hands. It had open interest of 8,020. With the stock up, the option fell 1-7/8 to 1-1/2.
Other active puts included the November 130 and 120.
Trading in the December, January and April series was quiet.
